Town tab mock-up

M1 slices S2, S3 and S5. S2 (built): the header, the stock bar, the Town tab, the build sheet and the building sheet, drawn at 412 px and 360 px before it was built.

Slices S2 and S3 were approved on 2026-11-10; the People tab and the tab bar are on their own page (S4). Slice S5, the Village, comes first below, for approval now.

S5: the Village

Slice S5 lets the Hamlet become a Village, by your own tap, once it has 20 residents and 180 wood, 180 stone and 45 tools. Settlers now arrive and unhappy residents can leave. Two screens change: the Hall row on the Town tab, and the away card. These are screenshots of the real app at 412 px and 360 px, with a working prototype of S5. Its code is kept back until you approve this page.

Pictures B to F show the soak's scripted player's own town, as the prototype engine made it: ready to order at year 2, season 3, day 5, hour 16, and a Village 4 game days later. Picture G is set up by hand. Tap a picture to zoom.

A. A new Hamlet: what is missing

The row now says what the Hamlet is, its residents and lots, then what the Village gives and costs. While it cannot be ordered the button is off, and every missing thing is listed: residents first, then stock.

A2. Enough residents, short of stock

The scripted player's town when its 20th resident arrived. Only the stock line shows.

B. Ready to order

25 residents, the Hamlet's limit, and the stock for it. The button is lit.

C. It asks first

The cost is paid at once and work at the front of the queue cannot be stopped, so the tap asks in the row. "Not yet" closes the question and changes nothing.

D. Under way

The stock is paid, the button is gone, and the row and the queue both show the work.

D2. Waiting behind other work

Set up by hand: the same ready town with the camp's upgrade already under way. The Hall's order waits, and the queue offers Cancel, as for any waiting job. Cancelling gives the stock back as far as the stores have room; anything over a cap is lost. Once the work starts it cannot be stopped.

E. A Village

The header says Village, the Hall is tier 2 with room for 60, and 4 new empty lots open: 10 in all. The Village is the Hall's last tier in this milestone, so there is no button.

F. The away card

The same town, closed for 130 game hours just after ordering. The card gains "Arrived" with the settlers' names, and the Village shows under "Finished". A Village also catches up at most 960 game hours (40 game days, two nights away) where a Hamlet catches up 480; that changes no screen.

G. Someone left (alert state)

Set up by hand: 9 residents, one of them at morale 0, a second Cottage and 100 food, closed 30 game hours. Dai leaves at the start of the game day and Llew arrives. "Left" is in ember. Nobody ever leaves a town of 8 or fewer, and at most one leaves a season (D-025).

For you to decide (the build's open items)

  • While the Hall's work runs, the row reads "Becoming a Village, N left" in place of the button, and the queue names it "The Hall to Village" (it said "The Hall to tier 2").
  • With both residents and stock missing, both lines show, residents first, as "Needs 20 residents" (the spec's wording) rather than "12 more"; the count sits just above.
  • "Upgrade to Village" asks first, in the row (C). It is the dearest order in the game and cannot be stopped once it starts. One tap more.
  • The away card has "Arrived" and "Left" rows with names, and the Village under "Finished" as "The Hall: now a Village".

Other choices drawn here

  • The Hall row's first line adds the tier's name and its lots: "Hamlet · Residents 8 / 25 · 6 lots".
  • The "Needs" lines are in ember, as on the building sheet.
  • A staffed Tavern now shows among every resident's morale reasons as "The tavern +4", +4 for each worker there, up to +12. No picture: no screen changes for it.

S3: production methods and the away card

Change round 1 (2026-11-10). Morgan asked that a method a building has not had before costs stock as well as time, once; after that, switching to it is quicker and free. A bought method belongs to its building. This page is redrawn for that.

Slice S3 adds two things. The building sheet lists every method for a building, so you can switch between them. A card at the top of the Town tab says what happened while the app was closed. These are screenshots of the real app, at 412 px and 360 px, with a working prototype of S3. The prototype was thrown away afterwards, and S3's code is written only after you approve this page.

A. The Mine's methods

Each method shows what it makes and uses, per worker, each game day. "In use" marks the current one. Dig ore and Quarry stone are owned from the start, so Quarry stone offers a free Switch. A method the Mine has not bought shows its price; tier 2 ones show their tier until the Mine is upgraded. The town is set up by hand for the picture: a Mine built at day 2, hour 8, with 12 ore in store.

B. Switching asks first

Tapping Switch asks in the sheet, because even a free switch stops work for 4 game hours. The question has a plain border; ember is kept for what is short or wrong.

C. While it retools

After the switch, the Mine is on Quarry stone and makes nothing for 4 game hours. Quarry stone reads "In use, retooling". Retooling is a cost the player chose, so it is shown in plain text.

The lot row on the Town tab says the same.

D. Buying a method

A new Workshop owns only Mend and make do. Forge tools costs 20 wood and 10 stone, once, and then 1 game day to set up. Buy and Switch look the same in the list; the question's own button carries the lamp-amber. When the stock is short, Buy is off and says what is missing ("Needs 10 stone"). The Workshop's 46 wood, 14 stone and 18 ore are set up by hand for the picture.

Just after buying: 20 wood and 10 stone are gone, Forge tools reads "In use, retooling" for 1 game day, and Mend and make do reads "Owned". The clearing line now says the bought method would be lost.

E. A Workshop short of ore (alert state)

The Workshop is set to Forge tools but has no ore, so it works by Mend and make do. The sheet names the input that is missing. Once ore arrives, it forges again with no tap. The log says once that it ran short.

F. The away card

This town was closed for 100 game hours. Its Workshop was on Forge tools with no ore, and a Woodcutter's camp was 6 game hours from done. Every number on the card is what the prototype engine actually produced. "1 tools" is how the app already writes amounts ("Needs 5 tools").

Choices drawn here that the spec left open

  • Prices to buy a method, all my estimate (S5's scripted player will show whether the Village still comes in time): Forge tools 20 wood, 10 stone. Tier 2: Snares and baskets 20 wood, 5 tools; Iron ploughs 30 wood, 10 tools; Saw pit 30 wood, 5 tools; Timbered shafts 40 wood, 5 tools; Cut-stone quarry 30 wood, 10 tools; Water-wheel hammer 40 wood, 30 stone, 10 tools. Tier 3: Smokehouse 50 wood, 20 stone, 10 tools; Crop rotation 60 wood, 30 stone, 15 tools; Managed coppice 60 wood, 20 stone, 15 tools.
  • The six methods with no inputs cost nothing and every building owns its own from the start: Gather, Hand plots, Hand axes, Dig ore, Quarry stone, Mend and make do.
  • Setting up a bought method takes 1 game day; switching to an owned one takes 4 game hours, one production cycle.
  • Clearing a lot loses what its building bought; the clearing question says so.
  • Switching or buying asks first in the sheet. One tap more each time.
  • A short building's lot row reads "Forge tools · Short: Mend and make do" in ember, so you see both what you chose and what is really running. The sheet says "In use, short" and "Short of ore: running Mend and make do".
  • Retooling is shown in plain text.
  • "Uses" lists resources in the stock bar's order (wood before ore), as costs already do.
  • Mend and make do still offers Switch while the Workshop is short. Switching to it costs 4 game hours of work and changes nothing until ore comes back, but it is the player's call.
  • The card is called "While you were away". It shows how long you were gone, and has three lines: Made, Finished, Ran short. A line with nothing to show is left out, except Made, which says "Nothing". The time a building ran short is in game days and hours. Losses (a full store) and what was used up are not on the card; the stock bar shows the result.
  • The card appears after a catch-up of 10 game hours or more. It stays until you tap Dismiss, or until the next such catch-up replaces it. A reload drops it.
  • The card sits at the top of the Town tab, above the Hall.

Choices drawn here that the spec left open

  • The stock bar is 4 cells across, as the style doc says, so the fifth resource (Tools) sits alone on a second row. Five across would fit one row but makes each cell about 70 px wide at 412 px.
  • No tab bar yet. The style doc shows only tabs that work, and the People tab arrives in S4.
  • The Hall row shows "Residents 8 / 25" so the town's size is on screen before the People tab exists.
  • A job that has not started reads "Waiting, takes 1 game day"; its lot reads "Waiting in the work queue".
  • The Tavern can be built from S2 but does nothing until S5, when morale arrives. Its line says only "Work for 1".
